title: Ordinary complete direct image agrees with its specified finite-image Roos limit
statement: Let ell be prime, E/Q_ell a finite normed extension, h:T→U any scheme morphism, and c_A:h^{-1}A_U≅A_T the canonical completed coefficient comparison of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Let K be an arbitrary derived-complete complex in the detailed completed integral module category of [def-weil-derived-complete]. Suppose the product of its restricted finite direct-image terms exists. For every chosen Roos-limit object L of that tower, with the transitions prescribed by [def-weil-derived-direct-image], ordinary derived direct image of K after the normalized coefficient transport is isomorphic to the coefficient transport of L. No boundedness, constructibility, geometric base or properness assumption is required.

source.place: Lemmas 4.2.12, 6.5.9, 6.5.11, 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15; the corresponding step of lem-weil-pbc-realization-localized-push

proof.text: First compare the canonical completed structural map with the detailed structural map after the normalized coefficient isomorphisms. On each finite projection this is naturality of the constant-sheaf comparison and the prescribed quotient lift. Equality follows by joint monicity of the inverse-limit projections. The resulting identity on sections is linear, so it gives the ordinary direct-image/restriction square. Exact coefficient restriction is an equivalence; deriving the square gives the corresponding comparison on ambient derived direct images.

Countable products of pro-etale module sheaves are exact. The derived localization Q therefore preserves them. Represent a family by K-injective complexes; their termwise product is K-injective by right orthogonality. The derived-functor units on the factors and product identify the image product with the product of derived images. Ordinary completed module direct image preserves products because its underlying additive presheaf is precomposition. Thus its total right derived functor preserves countable products.

Map the completeness Roos triangle through this triangulated product-preserving functor. Its one-minus-shift arrow becomes the one-minus-shift of the image tower. The specified sfDerivedRestrictionComparison isomorphisms transport its terms and transitions to sfDirectImageTerm and sfDirectImageTransition by their definitions. The derived-limit morphism theorem and levelwise-isomorphism criterion compare this Roos object with every given SfIntegralDirectImage. Compose with the derived coefficient square from the first step.
